note: First-reading proposals the second reading judged unnecessary. Kept for the record; no change proposed.

withdrawn.hebrew: וְיָדְעוּ כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם לְשָׁכְנִי בְתוֹכָם אֲנִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵיהֶם׃
withdrawn.english: They shall know that I am YHWH their God, who brought them out of Egypt to dwell among them. I am YHWH their God.

first_reading.proposed: They shall know that I am YHWH their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt to dwell among them. I am YHWH their God.
first_reading.reason: מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם is "out of the land of Egypt"; אֶרֶץ ("land of") is left untranslated, though the column renders it elsewhere.

second_reading.note: אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם and 'Egypt' name the same place; 'out of Egypt' for מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם is idiomatic compression that loses no meaning.

withdrawn.hebrew: הַקָּהָל חֻקָּה אַחַת לָכֶם וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם כָּכֶם כַּגֵּר יִהְיֶה לִפְנֵי יְהוָה׃
withdrawn.english: For the assembly there shall be one statute for you and for the resident alien who lives with you, an enduring statute throughout your generations. You and the resident alien shall be alike before YHWH.

first_reading.proposed: For the assembly there shall be one statute for you and for the resident alien who sojourns, an enduring statute throughout your generations. You and the resident alien shall be alike before YHWH.
first_reading.reason: English adds "with you". The Hebrew here has only וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר ("and for the alien who sojourns"); אִתְּכֶם ("with you") stands in v.16, not in v.15, so the verse is assimilated to the next one.

second_reading.note: וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר needs a complement in English; 'with you' is the implied sense (אִתְּכֶם in 15:14, 16) and JPS supplies it too.

withdrawn.hebrew: וַתֵּרָגְנוּ בְאָהֳלֵיכֶם וַתֹּאמְרוּ בְּשִׂנְאַת יְהוָה אֹתָנוּ הוֹצִיאָנוּ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם לָתֵת אֹתָנוּ בְּיַד הָאֱמֹרִי לְהַשְׁמִידֵנוּ׃
withdrawn.english: You grumbled in your tents and said: Because YHWH hates us, He brought us out of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us.

first_reading.proposed: You grumbled in your tents and said: Because YHWH hates us, He brought us out of the land of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us.
first_reading.reason: מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם (me-eretz Mitsrayim) is 'from the land of Egypt'; אֶרֶץ ('land of') is not rendered.

second_reading.note: מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם as 'out of Egypt' names the same place in idiomatic English; dropping אֶרֶץ changes nothing the verse says.

withdrawn.hebrew: וְרָם לְבָבֶךָ וְשָׁכַחְתָּ אֶת־יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הַמּוֹצִיאֲךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים׃
withdrawn.english: your heart become proud and you forget YHWH your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slaves,

first_reading.proposed: your heart become proud and you forget YHWH your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves,
first_reading.reason: מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם (me-eretz Mitsrayim) is 'from the land of Egypt'; אֶרֶץ ('land of') is not rendered.

second_reading.note: מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם as 'out of Egypt' names the same place in idiomatic English; dropping אֶרֶץ changes nothing the verse says.

withdrawn.hebrew: וְהִנֵּה אֶשְׁלַח אֶת־הַנַּעַר לֵךְ מְצָא אֶת־הַחִצִּים אִם־אָמֹר אֹמַר לַנַּעַר הִנֵּה הַחִצִּים מִמְּךָ וָהֵנָּה קָחֶנּוּ וָבֹאָה כִּי־שָׁלוֹם לְךָ וְאֵין דָּבָר חַי־יְהוָה׃
withdrawn.english: Then I will send the boy, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you,’ take him and come, for there is peace for you and no danger, as YHWH lives.

first_reading.proposed: Then I will send the boy, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; take them,’ then come, for there is peace for you and no danger, as YHWH lives.
first_reading.reason: קָחֶנּוּ ("take it") belongs to the words spoken to the boy and its suffix refers to the arrow(s); only וָבֹאָה ("then come") addresses David. "Take him and come" gives David an object the Hebrew lacks.

second_reading.note: קָחֶנּוּ has a singular suffix and joins וָבֹאָה by vav, so 'take him and come' addressed to David (like לֵךְ in 20:22) is a reading the Hebrew bears.

withdrawn.hebrew: וְעַתָּה לְעֵינֵי כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל קְהַל־יְהוָה וּבְאָזְנֵי אֱלֹהֵינוּ שִׁמְרוּ וְדִרְשׁוּ כָּל־מִצְוֺת יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם לְמַעַן תִּירְשׁוּ אֶת־הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה וְהִנְחַלְתֶּם לִבְנֵיכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם עַד־עוֹלָם׃
withdrawn.english: Now, before the eyes of all Israel, YHWH's assembly, and in the hearing of our God, keep and seek all the commandments of YHWH your God, so that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons after you forever.

first_reading.proposed: Now, before the eyes of all Israel, YHWH's assembly, and in the hearing of our God, keep and seek all the commandments of YHWH your God, so that you may possess the good land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons after you forever.
first_reading.reason: הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה is 'the good land'; there is no demonstrative (no הַזֹּאת). 'this good land' follows the KJV wording, not the Hebrew.

second_reading.note: The article of הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה is deictic for the land David stands in; 'this good land' (so JPS) is sound English, not a departure.

withdrawn.hebrew: וּכְנַף הַכְּרוּב הָאֶחָד אַמּוֹת חָמֵשׁ מַגִּיעַ לְקִיר הַבָּיִת וְהַכָּנָף הָאַחֶרֶת אַמּוֹת חָמֵשׁ דְּבֵקָה לִכְנַף הַכְּרוּב הָאַחֵר׃
withdrawn.english: [BHS 3:12] One wing of the other cherub, five cubits, reached the house's wall, and the other wing, five cubits, joined the wing of the other cherub.

first_reading.proposed: [BHS 3:12] The wing of the one cherub, five cubits, reached the house's wall, and the other wing, five cubits, joined the wing of the other cherub.
first_reading.reason: וּכְנַף הַכְּרוּב הָאֶחָד is 'the wing of the one cherub'; the English writes 'the other cherub' (as the KJV does), so both halves name 'the other cherub' where the Hebrew contrasts הָאֶחָד with הָאַחֵר.

second_reading.note: הָאֶחָד here resumes the second cherub of v.11 (correlative אֶחָד … אֶחָד); 'the other cherub', as in JPS, gives the Hebrew's sense in context.

withdrawn.hebrew: יֵרֵד כְּמָטָר עַל־גֵּז כִּרְבִיבִים זַרְזִיף אָרֶץ׃
withdrawn.english: May his word descend like rain upon mown vegetation, like showers dripping upon the earth.

first_reading.proposed: May he descend like rain upon mown vegetation, like showers dripping upon the earth.
first_reading.reason: יֵרֵד כְּמָטָר: 'may he (the king) descend like rain'. 'His word' is not in the Hebrew; it is an interpretive gloss (as in Rashi) supplied as the subject.

second_reading.note: יֵרֵד has no expressed subject; 'his word' is Rashi's reading (יֵרֵד דְּבָרוֹ), which the Hebrew can bear, so the column's rabbinic priority covers it.

withdrawn.hebrew: מִהַר צֹעֶה לְהִפָּתֵחַ וְלֹא־יָמוּת לַשַּׁחַת וְלֹא יֶחְסַר לַחְמוֹ׃
withdrawn.english: The one girded with strength will quickly be loosened; his captive will not die in destruction or lack bread.

first_reading.proposed: The one girded with strength will quickly be loosened; he will not die in destruction or lack bread.
first_reading.reason: וְלֹא־יָמוּת לַשַּׁחַת has no new subject: the same צֹעֶה who is loosened 'will not die'. 'His captive' is added with no Hebrew word behind it and shifts who is spared.

second_reading.note: With צֹעֶה kept as the girded oppressor who is loosened, וְלֹא־יָמוּת must concern his victim; the proposal would promise life and bread to the oppressor.
